blocks.text: Lackner prices set beside the rest of Richmond

Lackner houses are in the upper third of the city: 7th of 21 Richmond sub-areas with ten or more house sales, at a $1,765,000 median. Woodwards is $7,500 above it ($1,772,500, 22 sales) and Steveston Village is $3,000 below ($1,762,000, 20 sales), so the three are within $10,500 of each other. Lackner buyers got closer to asking than in most places: 96.0% of the last list price, 5th highest of the 21 areas, with 5% of houses selling above list.

The lots are small and the houses middle-aged. The median Lackner lot is 4,809 square feet, the 4th smallest of 21 areas, and the median house was built in 1990. At $672 a square foot the $1,765,000 median implies about 2,630 square feet of house, a rough figure, as dividing one median by another is only approximate. Half of all sales landed between $1,600,000 and $2,145,000, a band $545,000 wide that is the 12th widest of 21 areas, which puts Lackner about mid-table for how far apart its sale prices were.

The quarterly house medians were $1,972,500 in November to January (6 sales); $1,650,000 in February to April (7 sales); $1,826,500 in May to July (6 sales). The last quarter in the MLS® data had too few Lackner sales to quote, and with only six or seven sales in each of the others the swings between them are within what a handful of different houses would produce.

Townhomes were few, 7 sales in the year, so the figures are indicative only: a $1,104,000 median, 25 days to sell, 94.0% of the last list price and 14% sold over list. The median strata fee was $400 a month and the median build year 2000, ten years newer than the median Lackner house.

items.t: City-wide, single-family and duplex lots were rezoned in June 2024 into RSM/S, RSM/M, RSM/L or RSM/XL zones for small-scale multi-unit housing, assigned by prior zone and lot size; about 84% of affected lots were RS1/A, RS1/B or RS1/E. Which zone applies to a given Lackner lot needs a parcel check.

faq.q: What did homes in Lackner sell for?
faq.a: The median house sale in Lackner was $1,765,000, across 21 sales from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: How long do homes take to sell in Lackner?
faq.a: Half sold in 22 days or less, at a median 96.0% of the last list price; 5% went over asking (sales from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026).

faq.q: What price range do most houses in Lackner sell in?
faq.a: The middle half of the 21 houses that sold in Lackner went for between $1,600,000 and $2,145,000, around a median of $1,765,000.

faq.q: Do houses in Lackner sell above asking price?
faq.a: 5% of the 21 houses sold for more than the last list price, and the median sale was 96.0% of it.

faq.q: How old are the houses that sold in Lackner?
faq.a: The median year built was 1990 for the 21 houses sold in Lackner.

faq.q: How many bedrooms do houses in Lackner usually have?
faq.a: The median house that sold in Lackner had 5 bedrooms, from the 21 sales between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: How big are the lots in Lackner?
faq.a: The median lot among houses that sold was 4,809 square feet, about 0.11 acre. That is the 4th smallest median of the 21 Richmond areas with ten or more house sales.

faq.q: Do Lackner houses sell close to asking?
faq.a: Yes, compared with the rest of Richmond. The median sale was 96.0% of the last list price, 5th highest of 21 areas, and 5% of the 21 houses sold above list.

faq.q: Do I need a home inspection when buying in Richmond?
faq.a: It is strongly recommended. Make the offer subject to an inspection so a qualified inspector can look at the roof, structure, drainage, electrical and heating before you remove conditions.
